selection_rationale: Portugal is an EU, euro-area and NATO member whose fiscal repair, Atlantic geography, renewable-heavy power system, tourism-dependent external balance and migration-supported labour supply create mechanisms not covered by existing France, Germany or European security dossiers. A reusable Portuguese country context is needed to analyse Iberian energy integration, Atlantic logistics and defence, southern-European productivity convergence and the post-RRF investment transition without reconstructing the same structural background.
contrary_evidence: Sharp public-debt reduction, repeated fiscal surpluses, historically low unemployment and stronger bank balance sheets support a resilience thesis, while debt remains high, ageing pressures are rising and productivity convergence remains weak.

Immigration has reversed population decline and expanded labour supply, while a very high ageing index and slower migration in 2025 show that demographic constraints have been mitigated rather than solved.

Renewables already supply most electricity consumption and can support industrial investment, while imported fuels, system-integration needs and the Iberian blackout demonstrate that electricity abundance is not equivalent to complete energy autonomy.

Housing price increases are extreme, but limited mortgage-credit expansion and stronger banks indicate that structural supply restrictions are currently a clearer mechanism than a repeat of the pre-2011 credit cycle.
limitations: Portugal revised its 2021–2025 population series using a new administrative-data methodology, so demographic comparisons must use consistent vintages.
Second-quarter 2026 GDP was revised after the flash estimate; observed quarterly data and annual forecasts are kept separate.
PRR milestone completion and payment requests do not directly measure completed productive capital or long-run productivity effects.
Housing transaction prices and new-contract rents do not by themselves measure affordability.
Renewable electricity shares cannot be extrapolated to total final energy consumption.
The ENTSO-E blackout report describes a multi-factor interconnected-system event and should not be reduced to a single-country or single-technology cause.
The NATO 2% accounting measure does not directly measure operational readiness or domestic defence-industry output.

Revision 1 corrects the Q2 2026 year-on-year GDP figure to the current INE value of 2.5% and adds the required evidence-bearing geographic map in both locales; the broader analytical thesis is unchanged.

en.title: Portugal: fiscal repair, migration-led labour supply and the productivity test after the recovery-fund cycle
en.deck: Portugal has cut public debt sharply, reached historically low unemployment and built a renewable-heavy electricity system, but productivity, housing and ageing will determine whether post-PRR growth produces durable convergence in living standards.
en.regime: Fiscally repaired, services-heavy euro-area economy with strong labour demand, migration-supported population growth and renewable electricity, approaching a post-recovery-fund transition in which productivity and housing supply become decisive.
en.key_risk: Exceptional EU-funded investment fades while productivity remains weak, housing costs stay elevated and migration slows, leaving ageing and higher defence expenditure to compete for a narrower fiscal and labour base.

pt-BR.title: Portugal: reparação fiscal, oferta de trabalho impulsionada pela imigração e o teste de produtividade após o ciclo dos fundos de recuperação
pt-BR.deck: Portugal reduziu fortemente a dívida pública, alcançou desemprego historicamente baixo e construiu um sistema elétrico com forte participação renovável, mas produtividade, habitação e envelhecimento determinarão se o crescimento após o PRR produzirá convergência durável do padrão de vida.
pt-BR.regime: Economia da área do euro fiscalmente reparada e intensiva em serviços, com forte demanda por trabalho, crescimento populacional sustentado por migração e eletricidade renovável, entrando em uma transição pós-fundos de recuperação na qual produtividade e oferta habitacional se tornam decisivas.
pt-BR.key_risk: O investimento excepcional financiado pela UE diminui enquanto produtividade continua fraca, habitação permanece cara e migração desacelera, deixando envelhecimento e maior gasto de defesa disputar uma base fiscal e de trabalho mais estreita.
